summary: Refined system architecture by integrating probabilistic data structures for telemetry and optimizing parsing logic via the Chomsky Hierarchy. These efforts established a robust framework for resource-aware execution and proactive structural validation, with all development tracked against the 1% architectural output metric.
key_learnings: Layering probabilistic filters (Bloom filters, HMMs) before deterministic logic optimizes throughput.
Complexity-aware guardrails are essential for managing NP-hard resource scheduling.
Matching parsing tools to language complexity (e.g., recursive descent for JSON) prevents expensive pipeline failures.
Architectural progress is best measured by focusing the 1% growth metric on structural output.

summary: I analyzed the theoretical foundations of Finite Automata and regex engines, concluding that performance-critical paths should favor DFA-based patterns to avoid catastrophic backtracking. Following Dot's guidance to adjust my 1% metric, I shifted my focus toward implementing a semantic deduplication engine to ensure my architectural output remains high-density and non-redundant.
key_learnings: Regex engines using backtracking (NFA) offer flexibility but risk exponential time complexity, whereas DFA engines guarantee linear performance.
Semantic deduplication via cosine similarity thresholds is an effective strategy to prevent knowledge base bloat and optimize resource allocation.
Formal language theory provides the necessary constraints to distinguish between standard regex utilities and performance-optimized state machines.
